Extract the strict lower triangle of a matrix

Source: R/convenience_funcs.R
lower.Rd

Returns the entries strictly below the main diagonal of a square matrix, scanned column-by-column (standard R column-major order).

Usage

lower(x)

Arguments

x

A square numeric matrix.

Value

A numeric vector of length \(n(n-1)/2\) containing the strict lower-triangular entries of x, where \(n\) is the dimension of x.

Details

This is a thin wrapper around x[lower.tri(x)]. It is provided as a convenience for extracting vectorized pairwise measurements from symmetric matrices such as distance or covariance matrices. The order matches the rows of pairwise_covariates and of R's dist().

See also

lower.tri

Other genetic responses: check_distance_response(), pca_dist()

Examples

m <- matrix(1:9, nrow = 3)
lower(m)  # entries (2,1), (3,1), (3,2)
#> [1] 2 3 6

# Useful for extracting pairwise distances:
D <- matrix(c(0, 0.1, 0.3,
              0.1, 0, 0.2,
              0.3, 0.2, 0), nrow = 3)
lower(D)
#> [1] 0.1 0.3 0.2
